_comment: The learner's path through the Part 1 launch (task1), in one place. task1/scripts/course_path.py projects it into the notebooks (the strip under each title, the card after each '## Next' cell, the map on 00_Home.ipynb, the milestone tag); course_ui.py reads it at run time for the course bar and the Home card. Minutes follow the 2026-11-02 plan with two changes of 2026-11-04: VSS Coding Agent Skills takes 40 minutes (it was 25), so Part 1 is 195 with a 10-minute break, and lunch takes 45 minutes (it was 60), so no Part 2 time moves. Introduction 30, lunch 45, Part 2 210 on its own launch (task2), 480 in all. Paths are relative to /dli/task. 'kind' is notebook, terminal, assessment, slides, break or lunch; only the first three count as steps. 'block' is the part of the day. 'summary' is the one line the map, the bar and the previous step's card show; 'needs_before' and 'done_when' are shown in the notebook; 'grades' is the sentence the card two steps before an assessment shows. 'course_docs' marks a step whose instructions are a Course Docs page, not a notebook: the page's source under docs/, whose H1 is the step's title. Such a step has no path and no milestone cell, and the generated cells tell learners to open Course Docs from the JupyterLab Launcher. Progress: a counted step is done once its milestone cell has run without an error in the saved notebook, or once a file matching one of its 'evidence' globs (relative to /dli/task) exists, and every counted step before it is done with it; an assessment is done only when its grader marker /dli/assessment_results/<id>.json says passed.

steps.title: VSS presentation (slides)
steps.summary: The instructor introduces VSS and the building blocks you use today.

steps.title: 0. Course Onboarding
steps.summary: Get to know JupyterLab, check that the lab is ready, and sign in to the coding agent.
done_when: the readiness check in 0.3 prints `READY TO CONTINUE`

steps.title: 1. Inspect VSS Deployment
steps.summary: See which services and models run here, check that they answer, and read the detector's labels.
done_when: the cell in 1.3 that reads the detector's labels prints the label list

steps.title: 2. RT-CV: Detection & Tracking
steps.summary: Add a video to VIOS, read RT-CV's detections from Kafka and Elasticsearch, and find the vehicles that stand still.
done_when: the check cell of the exercise in 2.11 prints how many cars pass your rule

steps.title: 3. RT-VLM: Captioning & Prompting
steps.summary: Caption the clip with RT-VLM and see how the chunk size, the sampled frames and the prompt change the answer.
done_when: the check cell of the exercise in 3.6 prints `PASS`

steps.title: 4. RT-Embed: Video Search
steps.summary: Search four traffic videos, write queries like captions, score the search against labels, and search one file at a time.
needs_before: the lab pill is green, which means the four search videos are indexed
done_when: the check cell of the exercise in 4.9 prints `PASS`

steps.title: Part 1 Assessment
steps.summary: On your own: use the building blocks on a new 30-second clip, answer eight questions, and submit.
done_when: the Submit cell shows PASSED and you have clicked ASSESS TASK on the course page
steps.grades: On your own, you use VIOS, RT-CV, Kafka, Elasticsearch and RT-VLM on a new clip, search the four traffic videos with RT-Embed, then answer eight questions.

steps.title: VSS Coding Agent Skills
steps.summary: Have a coding agent with the VSS skills process four traffic videos, report possible collisions with clip links, and watch a live stream for a collision.
done_when: Checkpoint 1 of the page: the coding agent has added the four videos under `agent_` names, extracted their metadata and reported possible collisions with VIOS clip links, and you have checked one clip against the report
Checkpoint 2: RT-VLM has watched the live stream `agent_collision_live`, and you have opened a clip of its alert from the VIOS recording, or read why no alert came

steps.title: Lunch
steps.summary: Save your work with Save HTMLs on the Home page. Then, on the course page, click STOP TASK for Part 1 and START for Part 2. Only one lab runs at a time.

steps.title: Part 2: Applying VSS to Traffic Anomalies
steps.summary: On its own launch: you deploy VSS for traffic anomalies, generate synthetic data, and fine-tune the Cosmos 3 Nano verifier. Then you deploy the fine-tuned model, have the coding agent evaluate VSS, and take the Part 2 assessment.
